utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. A very good afternoon to everybody. May we please hear the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. This is case number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the appearances on this 111th day of this case for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian, Ann Sutherland, and Ruth Karper for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Branko Lukic, John Ostojic, and Danilo Cirkovic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we start, may I please hear, do you have already a, not proffers, but a list of the witnesses to appear during next week, including Monday the following week?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Yes, we do. The witnesses, pursuant to our 65 ter submission, are as follows: 053, 066, 070, and 079. Witness number 070, at least via telephone through our investigator, has agreed to reschedule things so that he could appear before the Court on Friday and Monday of the following week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Witness 70. So we take it as granted that these witnesses will appear. In case there would be any obstacle or impediment, please let us know immediately that we can do the necessary. And we are also prepared to order the necessary related to those two witnesses you wanted us to order their appearance. They will appear hopefully as Chamber witnesses, and we didn't see any reason to order a subpoena because we don't have any indicia that they wouldn't come without this subpoena. We believe -- admittedly, I don't know the estimate of time related to the four witnesses you just mentioned. You believe that those four witnesses would cover the following six days.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We do, Your Honour. And based on prior history with respect to our witnesses, most recently this week, we may even anticipate that the one witness will go beyond the Monday and into the Wednesday, which was previously a holiday and now is not. But it all depends on the questions by the OTP and by the Court. Specifically, with respect to Witness 053, we believe that he will be lengthy and may take two to three days for his completion in its entirety, including questions emanating from the Defence, the anticipated cross-examination by the OTP, and the Court's potential questions. So we believe we can fulfil the entire six-plus days that the Court has requested us to bring witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It should only be quite clear from the outset that there won't be any hearing on Wednesday, because as I already stated yesterday, we all have our obligations and commitments, and therefore we should if possible in any event stick to the schedule, and this was not to have a hearing on Wednesday. And therefore, I think we appreciate very much that you undertook the necessary steps that we have these four witnesses, and let us please try that in both directions we can hear the witnesses on Friday and Monday, but on the other hand, not to go beyond this Monday. Anything else to be discussed before we start with -- or restart with our witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. We would just like to formally advise the Court that we did file a motion, as we suggested we would yesterday, in connection with the five witnesses that have experienced some personal dilemmas and problems, and we're not sure if the Court has received that motion, and I'm merely just providing you notice that we did file a written application and we believe we have sufficiently set forth pursuant to the Rules the basis upon which the videolink conference with the Court's discretion may proceed. We very specifically set forth their names. We filed it confidentially their 65 ter number and a brief summary of the basis as to why these witnesses cannot testify live here at The Hague but are willing nonetheless to testify via videolink. And we've also set forth the basis as required by the Rules as to the necessity of those the witnesses from the Defence perspective. And just to remind the Court respectfully, we believe the Court has previously agreed that these witnesses can be called. So they were on our initial list. And we continue to maintain that they're necessary and vital for the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And may I, therefore, invite the Prosecution to respond to this as soon as possible. Hopefully it's possible in oral form only, that we don't need the answer in writing, and that we can take the necessary measures if we can come to the conclusion that a videolink is the appropriate way to hear these witnesses as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have not yet received the motion, but we will review it as soon as we receive it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: From the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I then ask the usher to escort the witness into the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Vuleta. Please take your seat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I do hope that in the late afternoon or even evening of yesterday we did not confuse you with all these pictures of models. Unfortunately, we had no chance at all to be there ourselves and to visit these buildings on the spot, which no doubt would facilitate our work. But please continue as you did yesterday with your testimony. And it's for me under the Rules just to remind you that you are still under solemn declaration as it was yesterday. So may I ask the Defence to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Ostojic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Vuleta.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once again, I'd like to first apologise for yesterday evening and the difficulty I seem to have had in terms of expressing myself in connection with some of the exhibits that were put forth. But today I'm going to try to ask you some questions and then hopefully I'll go back to some of the exhibits so that we could clarify some points necessary for the Defence. Are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday you discussed the drinking water that was provided at the iron ore mine and that there was a special water well located at Donja Lamovita, which was 5 or 6 kilometres away from the facility that was shown to you on the picture S15.2. Correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yes. Yes, from the restaurant that was being shown me and the place, the hall where the vehicles belonging to the mine were parked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, was part of your duties and responsibilities to maintain and service this special water well in Donja Lamovita so that persons at the iron ore mine could use and be provided with drinking water?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The well was of major importance, and I had to devote most of my attention to it so as not to have any shortages or any cuts in water supply.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just so I understand your testimony, you would actually leave the area that was depicted that we saw yesterday on Exhibit S15-2 -- you would leave that area and go 5 or 6 kilometres to the actual special water well in order to maintain and service that water well; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the duties and responsibilities that you described in connection with maintenance and service of this special water well, those are the same duties and responsibilities that you performed before the attack on Prijedor as well as after the attack on Prijedor; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I maintained the drinking water well in the same way before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sometimes lawyers have to be a little more specific, so I'm going to ask you a question in connection with that. Specifically, sir, during the time period that you shared with us, the end of May 1992 through August of 1992, did you continue to maintain and service this special water well so that the detainees who were at the iron ore mine were able to be provided with drinking water?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also told us yesterday that you worked a 24-hour shift. During that 24 hours, sir, did you utilise the drinking water that you were maintaining and servicing for the people at the iron ore mine, during the period of May through August 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also drank that. Not always. At times I'd bring water from home, because we had a problem before the war. There was an outbreak of epidemics and a number of our workers fell ill. Some of them were in the hospital. While, I was lucky and did not succumb. But after these epidemics, the mine management distributed mineral water to us, and then special teams came from laboratories to do some chemical tests and they added something -- they added some chemicals and things. The water wasn't quite right either biologically or chemically. And there is documentation to this effect and analysis, and I believe it can still be found in the mine archives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When was that, sir? When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened -- I mean, the epidemics, it was before the outbreak of war, at the time when the situation was regular. Now, I don't exactly know when was that. It could have been 1990 or perhaps 1989. I do not know the exact day, but it was a long time before the war. Nobody even imagined that there would be a war at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so that we're clear, when you say "before the war," you're not referring to the war that commenced in Prijedor. You're talking about the war in Slovenia and Croatia. So somewhere between 1989 and 1990; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes. Yes, yes. Before any conflict, either in Slovenia -- no, nobody could even dream that there would be a war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me switch the topic from water to food now. You mentioned yesterday at pages 80 and on, you discussed the cafeteria that you identified on Exhibit S15-2 and then you also mentioned another restaurant and a kitchen which was near the separation where all the food was prepared. And for the Court and counsel, that's on page 81. And you also mentioned that that cafeteria, the other one, and kitchen were approximately 2 kilometres east of the photograph that we were discussing yesterday evening. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's a slight error there. The kitchen, that is, where food was cooked, was east of the cafeteria where it was distributed. And we called it Kop, that is, to the east where the -- was the restaurant with cooking facilities and to the west was the cafeteria, where food was distributed to the workers at the time when the mine worked, and then later on the place where the detainees were also distributed food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so that I may have clarification. On the exhibit that we saw yesterday, there was the cafeteria; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the cafeteria where in the spring and summer of 1992 the detainees would be provided with food?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the food prepared in that cafeteria that we saw on the exhibit or was it prepared in a different cafeteria, as you described it, 2 kilometres east and then that food being prepared was brought to the cafeteria?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, actually, sir, I gave you an option on the question. I used the word "or," so let me just clarify it. It's true, isn't it, that in fact the food was prepared for the detainees in the spring and summer of 1992 in a different facility 2 miles east from the area that was depicted in the exhibit and it was brought to the cafeteria that you identified and that is where the detainees ate that food; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vuleta, you having been working a 24-hour shift, did you also and likewise eat the same food that the detainees ate in the spring and summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took of the same food as the detainees, except because I also maintained the cooking facilities and I knew the personnel, I would get larger portions of the food. But the type of food was the same for the workers, for the detainees, and the troops. It was cooked the same way, using the same facilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe for us, please, the food that you ate during the period of summer 1992 that the detainees also ate.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the food was beans. One day we'd have potatoes, then rice. It depends. It wasn't the same food every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often in a given day was food being provided to the detainees in the spring and summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had only one meal a day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if bread was provided to the detainees at that time, the spring and summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. In the early days, they got a quarter of a loaf of bread. But as the time went by, they were getting an eighth part of a loaf because we were surrounded and cut off from Serbia and cut off from Croatia in the west, and since our supplies were running short, then we had to distribute what we had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it fair to say that there was less food being provided to everyone at the iron ore mine, including the detainees, as well as the employees, such as yourself, including the police force that was there, as well as the military force; correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask counsel to refrain from leading from now on in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Comments?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think, quite frankly, Your Honour, we've set a precedent here. And I'd hate to argue this rather, in my opinion, minuscule point, when if we review the transcript of any witness, and I don't say with any reservation, that this Court is allowed, at least with all the OTP witnesses they've been led, and there was not an open-ended question that they asked without it being led. But I can restate the question without any problem, but...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objection dismissed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vuleta, let me try the question again, in any event. The food that you said ultimately during the tenure of late May through August of 1992, it became -- the supplies were reduced. Did that apply just to the detainees?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the detainees -- I think -- I mean, I know that they were getting less. And as for the troops, I believe they had two meals. That is what I think. I didn't really go there, but I saw their food being poured out, distributed, taken away, army troops, detainees -- so I -- no, I still think that the army troops received two meals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about yourself and other employees of the iron ore mine? Did you also receive the main -- the same portions as you had prior to this reduction in supply?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when our supplies declined and the quality of food also declined, so I often brought my food from home so that I never even went to that kitchen. I would simply bring it along. Sometimes I did eat in the kitchen, but I -- I mean, I had enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me switch now from water and food to sleeping accommodations at the iron ore mine. During the spring and summer of 1992, did you, sir, during your 24-hour shift also sleep at or near the iron ore mine?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When on my shift, I slept in the electric workshop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you provided, sir, with a mattress and a pillow for your specific sleeping accommodations, or at the very least describe for us, so that I don't lead -- describe for us your personal sleeping accommodations during the time that you were at the iron ore mine from late May through late August 1992.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I and other workers who worked in the mine, I personally slept on a wooden table, on a work table. I brought a kind of a sponge mattress from home, and it was -- the weather was warm, so there was no need for me to cover with anything. But we had no beds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there beds anywhere within the iron ore mine complex in the spring and summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beds? No. There were no beds. I -- no. No, there were no beds there at all. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving right along. Yesterday on page 70 of your testimony you mentioned one of your superiors by the name of Mirko Babic. Do you remember that name, sir?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what Mirko Babic's title was in connection with the iron ore mine during the spring and summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirko Babic was the foreman in the workshop. He assigned jobs. He issued orders to me concerning work involving the electric installations or -- he also issued orders to locksmiths, what they had to do and so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of the police force during the spring and summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, come on. No. He was a civilian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just wanted to get clarification on that. Sir, was he a member of the military during the spring and summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Come, no. He was a civilian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he, sir, Mr. Babic, at any time during the spring and summer of 1992, when the detainees were at the iron ore mine, order, direct, or supervise any of the members of the police force that were present there?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirko Babic had nothing to do with the police. He merely organised work in the mine. He had nothing to do with the police or the army or anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. But it's my duty as an attorney to just clarify those factual issues. So just be patient with me. With respect to Mr. Babic, again, did he, sir, give any orders, commands, instructions, or supervise any members of the military at the iron ore mine in the spring and summer of 1992 when the detainees were present?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And may I add, in case you don't know, please say so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not aware that he could issue any orders to the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm, sir, looking for is specifically your personal observations and experiences. Did you, sir, at any time in the spring and summer of 1992 see or hear that Mr. Babic at any time ordered, commanded, instructed, or supervised any members of the military who were present at the iron ore mine in the spring and summer of 1992 while the detainees were there?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why, no. Mirko Babic had nothing to do with the military. I don't know what could he order.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With the assistance and permission of the Court, if the usher can show the witness Exhibit S15-2 again, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Vuleta, we're going to return to this exhibit that we spent some time yesterday and hopefully by utilising this one exhibit we can at least get some clarity on some issues, hopefully. Mr. Vuleta, I have a couple more questions in connection with this exhibit, S15-2. Specifically, if you can recall, based upon your personal objections, can you show us on this picture of a model prepared by the OTP where the police officers were stationed typically, on a typical day, in the spring and summer of 1992 while the detainees were there.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police was in this part, here. And it was police from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And just so the record is clear, if I may, Your Honour, the witness -- or Mr. Vuleta is indicating the picture -- by facing the picture, the building to the right -- on the right-hand side and immediately south of the building. He indicated the vacant area in front of that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in any other area were police force in existence?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were policemen in the administrative building too. I saw them there. And there were guards standing around here and here, around the buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, the witness has essentially encircled both -- or the building to the left, the large building, as well as the building to the north facing this picture, which I think is previously identified as a white house. And then the witness has also indicated that there were guards stationed around the entrance of the building which as we face is on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vuleta, to the best of your recollection, do you remember where the military personnel were stationed at or about the iron ore mine during the spring and summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military personnel were stationed -- well, I couldn't tell you the exact distance, but it was behind these buildings over there. There were some swamps there. And on this side there was a petrol station. So it was basically there was a ring -- there was military encircling the whole area.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think that adequately describes it, so I won't have to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, during the spring and summer of 1992, while the detainees were at the iron ore mine, did you carry a gun or a pistol or were you in any manner armed?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a civilian. I wore my work clothes, and I wore a white armband. I can't remember whether it was on my right or left arm, so that it was quite clear for all the guards to see that I was not one of the inmates.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I can, with the Court's permission and the assistance of the usher and the registry have the witness look at Exhibit S15-16.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to show you what's been previously marked as Exhibit S15-16 and ask you to please describe, if you can, the aerial side photograph of that picture. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This building is the white house. And while the mine was operating, this was where the roll call was read out for the miners. This building here was a pumper for sewage and the container. This here was the administration building and the canteen. The part up there was the administration building and down here was the canteen, where the workers had their meals. This here is a transformer station. This is a warehouse for lubricating oils. Then this building here -- you can't see it, but there were two buildings here. There was a pumping station here for sewage as well, and this is where there were high pressure pumps which were used to wash vehicles, to hose down vehicles when they were going to the mine and also the vehicles were washed here before being repaired. This building here we referred to as "the workshop." The western part of this building was where bulldozers and excavators and the trucks and other large vehicles were repaired. This part here, this was the garage and also a workshop for -- for dump trucks, and they were repaired here. And here there is a compressor station. Up here there were offices where various employees, technicians, engineers worked. I don't know if you're interested in anything else besides this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that's adequate for now. If the OTP or the Court has any other questions, I'm sure they're going to ask. Can you share with us, by looking at this exhibit, S15-16, during the spring and summer of 1992, when you were under your work obligation, where would you sleep during your 24-hour shift?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I slept in this area here, between this building and this part here. So it was right in the corner here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me just describe it if I can for the record. It's the larger of the two buildings by facing the picture on the right-hand side. And it's the area generally which is perpendicular section of that building to the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry. I don't want to interrupt you if not necessary, but on page 16, line 9 you said "the spring and summer of 1992, when you were under your work obligation." I don't have the impression following yesterday's transcript that we have already established when the work obligation started, whether it was in May or in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I could clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I thought it was clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you answer this question, sir, if I may, can you tell us when you were placed on a mandatory work obligation.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was placed under mandatory work obligation when the prisoners arrived in the mine. Before that, I was normally employed. But then instead of being recruited to go to the front line, I was left to work where I had been working and I was issued with a decision that this was my work obligation, to work in the Omarska mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what period of time was that, sir? Was it in May or August of 1992 -- or what period of time was it?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in May, but I can't be sure of the date. I think it may have been the 10th of May. I don't know the exact date, but I continued to work as usual. And later on I was issued with a decision that this was my mandatory work obligation and that I would not have to go to the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so that I clarify, with the Court's permission on the dates, it's my recollection, sir - and you please correct us, because we want to know what you recall - did you obtain this work obligation before or after the attack on Prijedor, as you described yesterday?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received it after that, when the prisoners arrived in the camp, when they first arrived. Maybe ten days after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. But just for clarity purposes, you mentioned just briefly approximately May 10th. The Court and counsel and I have been operating under the assumption that the attack on Prijedor happened May 30th of 1992. Would it be fair, sir, for purposes of clarity that you received your work obligation after the attack on Prijedor, which would have been after May 30th, 1992? Correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You're correct. I made a mistake. After their arrival -- that's right. I was a bit confused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as you stated yesterday, just so that it is clear, your work obligation continued, sir, beyond the spring and summer of 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. My work obligation continued. And after the prisoners left the mine, I was still under work obligation until 1995, when Sanski Most fell, when there was an attack. And then I was mobilised as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to turn to another issue, sir, and that involves a delegation that arrived in the second half of July 1992 at the iron ore mine. Can you tell us, sir, whether you have an independent recollection of a delegation from Banja Luka coming to the iron ore mine during the period of mid to late July 1992.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that a delegation arrived, but I didn't know where they'd come from or who they were. On that day I had a problem, if I may show you on this picture --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may interrupt. For my purposes, independent of your testimony --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If the usher, with the Court's permission, and show Mr. Vuleta Exhibit S15-2, so that he could show us exactly what he recalls. I think the witness may have --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vuleta. I apologise for interrupting. Again, can you show us on this picture, as you did yesterday, where the entrance to the iron ore mine was where this delegation came from. Point at it.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entrance was on the east side, on the eastern side, here, in the direction coming from Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry. I think the witness just told us that on that very day he had a problem, and I think it might be fair that -- for the witness to tell us what was the problem and to finalise his answer. Maybe then --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: -- all the other questions will be vacated. Mr. Vuleta, you wanted to tell us about a problem you had on that concrete day. Could you please continue, as you wanted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On that day, there was a problem because the external lighting had broken down. This was outside the buildings, around this edge here, around the perimeter. There were posts there with lighting, and I had a problem in this part here and here because the lights were out. On that day I worked to find the source of the problem. The transformer station is up here, and then cables run from the transformer station under the ground from post to post, and then they come up to here. So I set out to find out what had happened and why the lamps were out, so I went to look for the breakdown. I set out from the transformer station and followed the cables, and in this part here I found that a cable had been pierced between two posts. The cable was underground. I had to repair the damage, and I was unable to dig the cable up, so I had to go and find another piece of cable I could use to bridge this gap between these two posts. So I went and I found a piece of cable which I laid above ground in order to bypass the underground cable so that I could repair the lighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour? Just so the record is clear, with the Court's permission, can the witness identify with a marker the area that he was discussing where he was on or about the date that the Banja Luka delegation came.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we can describe it in a fair way. Please, it's for the parties to correct me if I'm wrong. In the beginning, the witness indicated that there was a problem concerning the entire area that is depicted as a grey area, and he wanted to find out the problem, which was somewhere between the main building, the white house, and the administrative building. And he found in front of the administrative building to the right-hand side of the model a problem where -- and he resolved the problem there in order to have the lights switched on in the entire area surrounding this administrative building. Would this be a fair description?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We're very grateful for the Court's assistance. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Vuleta, the section that the Court just identified on the lower right-hand corner, the section where this cable was separated and you were repairing, can you tell us, sir, when the Banja Luka delegation arrived, where were you physically present at the iron ore mine?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was right in this part where I was working, because it couldn't be done quickly. I was there until the afternoon, because I had to set out from the source of electricity and then check post by post until I found to where the breakdown had occurred. Then I had to go and fetch the cable. I had to lay it down. I had to connect it, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record, the witness hasn't said they were from Banja Luka. He said, "I didn't know where they'd come from or who they were."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objection sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's fair, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The group that came, as I identified them as a delegation - I apologise, Mr. Vuleta - the delegation that came that day while you were present on that day, can you tell us in which part they entered the iron ore mine. Did they come in on the same entrance that you've previously described for us?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The delegation entered from the east.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, sir, personally observe the delegation coming?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Two passenger cars drove in, and they stopped here, behind the administration building, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps not a big point, Your Honour. I think the witness said luksuzna and not "passenger," but luxury passenger vehicle. But in any event, we could check that later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the booths.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, very often this is synonymous. Witnesses often use -- say "luxury car," when they actually mean "passenger car." But he did say "luxury car," yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And then there was an objection?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Not an objection. I'd just like it marked for the record where he's pointing to.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm just curious from the comment how anyone can anticipate what a witness is thinking or not. The interpreter is saying very often witnesses are thinking this and meaning that. We'll discuss it at a later point, but if I could just proceed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No. I think it's quite clear. The interpreter assisted us by telling us that it's used as a synonym, luxury car or passenger car, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vuleta, can you tell us, having been there, the route in which the vehicles entering the iron ore mine in July of 1992, which route did they proceed upon entering into the complex, which route did they proceed to take?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The vehicles entered from the east, from the direction of Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just point at it for me again. I didn't have my picture --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point to the area again where the vehicles entered and then where they proceeded to go.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The vehicles entered from this direction and turned right, and they stopped here. I was working here repairing the breakdown. I saw that there was some sort of delegation, that they were gentlemen getting out of the cars. I knew Mr. Predrag Radic from Banja Luka, who was one of these people. I also knew Mr. Simo Miskovic and Simo Drljaca. I didn't know the others. And they went off behind the building and then they went off in this direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And just for the record and for the OTP the witness indicated that the vehicle upon entering the iron ore mine on the lower right-hand side made a right turn immediately before the building, at which point the cars were stopped. As the witness described, they got out of the car and then proceeded in a northerly direction by looking at that picture S15-2 and then proceeded left, which would be eastbound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the west here. Towards the west.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you very much. I think it's clear though. But just to make sure it's clear. The people who exited the vehicle, as you've described them, they proceeded northbound and then made a left that being westbound; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just going back a little bit. This delegation that you saw, how many people were in this delegation, sir?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were seven or eight people. The drivers remained in the cars. They stopped here. It was a very hot day, and it was shady here because this side is south. So most probably they stayed there in order to stay in the shade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, sir, on that day how far away were you from this delegation that arrived in mid -- or the second half of July 1992? How far away were you?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was very close to them. I didn't measure the distance, but it was some 3 or 4 metres away. I was here. It's not far.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you proceed to follow the delegation, sir, as they went westbound on the other side of this picture or building that's depicted on the picture S15-2? Did you continue to observe and follow them?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw when the delegation disappeared behind this corner. I continued doing my job. Why should I follow them? What mattered to me was to get my job done that had been assigned to me by my superior, and that was to solve the problem of the lighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know Dr. Milomir Stakic?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Dr. Milomir Stakic with this delegation in July of 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, Dr. Milomir Stakic was not in that delegation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us how long you have known Dr. Stakic and how it is that you met his acquaintance.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have known Dr. Stakic for a very long time. We were born in the same village. We weren't close neighbours. There were 5 or 6 kilometres between us. I first met Dr. Stakic before the war when we would see each other in the Tri Asa restaurant in Omarska. I remember very well he wore a black hat. His clothes were conspicuous. He had the long coat, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, at any time during the spring and summer of 1992, while you were there, did you observe or see Dr. Milomir Stakic at the iron ore mine?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never saw him during the period I worked there in the mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any doubt, sir, in your mind, based upon your personal observations, that had Dr. Milomir Stakic been with this delegation in July of 1992, that you would have recognised him?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm 100 per cent sure, and I can swear in a church or wherever you like that on that day Dr. Milomir Stakic wasn't there. If he had been, of course I would have recognised him. I would have said hello to him. But on that day, Dr. Stakic wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That's all we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is the Prosecution prepared to start the cross-examination immediately now, or should we have the break now?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I don't mind, Your Honour. I'm ready to start, or we can have an early break and then go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber stays adjourned until 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. May I ask the Prosecution to start their cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Ms. Sutherland:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vuleta, if you don't hear my question or you don't understand my question, can you please ask me to repeat it. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In May of 1992, were you working in the electrical workshop at the Omarska mine?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In May, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's the electrical workshop that's contained in what we described as the hangar building, and you pointed at that on Exhibit S15-2.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked on the entire mine system, and I would be in the workshop when I was off, and during the night that is where I slept.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right. And in the beginning of -- in May 1992, that is where your office was, where you pointed to it on that exhibit earlier today.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it was a workshop, not an office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said earlier at page 63 for counsel and the Chamber, that the mine stopped working when Prijedor was attacked. And we've established that that was on the 30th of May, 1992, when the non-Serbs tried to reverse the takeover of power. Is that correct, that the mine stopped working when Prijedor was attacked?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mine stopped with the exploitation of the ore, when the attack on Prijedor took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any detainees in Omarska camp before the 30th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, after. After.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it a fact that there were detainees in the Omarska camp before the 30th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you as certain about that as you are as certain about Dr. Stakic not being part of the delegation that you told us about just before we broke?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm going to object to the form of the question and to the sarcastic nature of the question, Your Honour. I think the witness's testimony speaks for itself. And I don't think that she should, in my opinion, respectfully weigh one thing or the other. If she has a point of contention with the witness, place it to the witness. But to place a question like that, in our opinion, is inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Maybe it can be appropriate to rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe I was being sarcastic, and I apologise to the witness if he took my question as that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you just said a moment ago that you saw no detainees in the camp and you were certain that there were no detainees in the camp prior to the 30th of May, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The detainees came after the attack on Prijedor and Kozarac, when the extremist groups attacked military columns.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit S353.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a nine-page document from the chief of the Prijedor police station, Simo Drljaca, and it's a report about "reception centres" in the municipality of Prijedor. Can I take you, please, to page 5. And that has the ERN number for the usher at the top of the page B0032582. And if the English could be placed on the ELMO. And it is page 4 of the English translation. Sir, looking at the third paragraph on that page, it talks about a Crisis Staff decision ordering that the Keraterm facility in Prijedor be used only for transit purposes. And then it goes on in the following paragraph - and I will read it for you - "pursuant to this decision, on 27 May 1992, all prisoners of war were transferred to Omarska." Do you still say that there were no prisoners -- no detainees in the Omarska camp prior to the attack on Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, let me object to the form of the question. And I also think it mischaracterise this witness's immediate prior testimony on page 27, lines 13 through 14. He specifically mentions Kozarac and an attack on the military convoy. This Court has restricted sometimes for us to discuss because it's hearsay events --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can you please stop arguing. I think we were -- we had agreed on the form of objections and in the way an objection has to be phrased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The objection is dismissed on the basis of previous transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, thank you. I've finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So you may proceed with the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, having taken you to that document, and it can be seen that detainees were transferred to the Omarska camp on the 27th of May, is it still your testimony that there were no detainees in Omarska prior to the attack on Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Dismissed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I did not make a record so as to be able to specify the date or the day. I know that it was when there was this attack on Prijedor. It was a long time ago. It's hard for me to remember whether it was on the 27th or on the 30th of May. But in any case, it was towards the end of May. I did not make any statistic so as to be able to know the day, the hour. It's very difficult to remember the exact day. I was -- I did not enter anything into a diary. I did not write a diary, so I don't know whether things happened on the 27th, the 30th, or the 1st. It was in that period of time. I was not authorised to run any records, to keep any records. I worked there, and it's very difficult for me to know the exact date. I am not in the position to -- to give you the exact dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to move now to Dr. Stakic. How do you know him? You said that he was from the same village as yourself and that he lived 5 to 6 kilometres away and that you would see him in the Tri Asa restaurant. Did you know him personally?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you please make reference to the point in transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It was the page before the break, just before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The parties are aware. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Page 24, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you know Dr. Stakic personally?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain it to you in more specific terms. I know him because we come from the same village. I know Mr. May because I saw him on TV. If I saw him in the street, I would recognise him. We come from the same village and obviously we knew each other. Secondly, Mr. Stakic married a woman whose sister married my neighbour. I know the parents of his wife, her brother's sisters, and we know each other. I know the villagers of my village. I am not intimate with them, but I know who is who, if you understand what I'm saying. I will know you when I see you on TV tomorrow, because I saw you. That means I met you. Is that enough?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Dr. Stakic have any siblings?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Dr. Stakic had a father whose name was Milan. His mother is Mira. She is from Kriva, from Sejici [phoen]. I think he has a brother. He doesn't have a sister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You think he has a brother. Do you know that person's name?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know his nickname is Baco. It is on the tip of my tongue. I know he worked in Germany. He drove a bus in Germany. I know that he is now married. He has two children. I can't remember his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is his brother's name Milorad Stakic?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I know that his nickname is Baco. That's what people call him. He was in Germany for a long time, and currently I don't know, I think he runs a department store in Prijedor. I haven't seen him in a long time. I saw him when he drove this bus to Germany, and that's where he was for quite a long time. I don't know exactly how long he was there. Milomir's father was a conductor in the bus that run from Maricka to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Dr. Stakic's brother, the one you call Baco, did he work in the iron ore mine at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ever have any other siblings?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only brother I know is this one. I don't know of any sisters that he had. I've never been to his house. I know where his house was. I didn't go into the house. I used to pass by because I know his neighbours, Vidak Stakic, Dusan Stakic, and the entire neighbourhood I know. But I have never been into his house nor was he ever in my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know a driver in the mine called Milorad Stakic?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I don't know what his name is, but his nickname is Mico. That's what we all call him. And what is his official name in the identity card, I don't know. I've never inspected his identity card. And amongst us worker, we used nicknames and we called him Mico. For example, my nickname was Vule. Nobody ever called me by my real name. We all had, so to say, our internal names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to move now to the delegation we were discussing just before the break. Do you recall anything --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry. In order that we don't have to come back to this area. You just mentioned, "I do know a driver in the mine called Milorad Stakic. I don't know what his name is, but his nickname is Mico." I really don't understand this answer. May I ask you what is the link for you between Mico and Milorad Stakic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It must be a mistake. There is only Mico Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So then once again, the question -- apparently it's not yet answered. Did you know a driver in the mine called Milorad Stakic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know any Milorad. I only know Mico Stakic. But I don't know whether in his identity papers his name is something else. We all call him Mico, if that is what we mean, what we have in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. Your testimony now is that indeed there were -- there was a person working there called Mico Stakic; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mico Stakic exists. He still exists. And he still works in the mine, Mico Stakic. That's what we workers call him. And what is written in his birth certificate, I don't know. We all call him Mico. If that is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. So you may proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question was: Did anything unusual -- do you recall anything unusual happening the day that you saw this delegation in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noticed and I heard songs. The detainees were singing Serbian songs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were the detainees who were singing these songs?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please show me the drawing, the map, the sketch, that is, and I'll show you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown document S15-2 once again and --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've got a fresh copy which I'll actually get the witness to mark, a fresh copy of Exhibit S15-2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let's proceed this way. But it's still the same document, S15-2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If you could just place that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I can see there is a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure if it's a problem. Just that the Court can engage me and explain while why we did the direct we were unable to have the witness mark a document but they can now. I mean, they can mark it. But just perhaps at another time the Court can just for my benefit and edification explain why when I asked the witness, the Court rejected my application. But let's proceed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I had the impression you appreciated the description and based on this description, it was satisfactory for the outcome and what you wanted to outline by your line of questions. But let's wait and see whether it's really necessary to have another document marked. We'll proceed on the basis of document S15-2, full stop. Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 11560 to 11573. Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. What's on the ELMO at the moment is a copy of S15-2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I am fully aware of this. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you said earlier today that -- can you please point on the ELMO machine where you were standing, where you were working.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was working here, in this part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you take --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Would Your Honour like the witness to mark this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think at the moment we should do it as we did it previously. The witness pointed at the same point. If you could describe it, please, for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you're pointing to the administration building -- the corner of the administration building. As we look at the photo, where the triangle is, at the bottom right-hand corner of the photograph, you're pointing to the side of the administration building nearest that triangle and you pointed in your evidence in chief, as I believe it -- as I understood it, to the corner of the administration building just before it goes into the restaurant -- cafeteria.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the east side. This is not where you go into the restaurant. You go into the restaurant from the west, if you get my meaning. This is the east here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know what's north, south, east, or west, but for the record is Your Honour clear where the witness has pointed? So it is the side of the -- near the cafeteria and the corner of the administration building away from the garages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that what you're -- is that where you're pointing to?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the east side of the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You're pointing to the side closest to the cafeteria of the administration building.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is not the nearest point to the cafeteria. The nearest point to the cafeteria is there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, just pause there.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here was -- these were the premises for the kitchen personnel and the cafeteria was over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, put your pointer back to where you were working.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the record, that is near to the corner of the administration building nearest to the cafeteria.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is that clear enough for the Defence and Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's in the middle of the right-hand side of the model we can see depicted on this picture. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Because we don't -- we shouldn't discuss in terms of north, east, south, and west. But I think it's fair to state that in the middle of the right-hand side; correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think he was pointing more to the top side, not -- not specifically right in the middle of the administration building. It was more towards the cafeteria.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We can see at this side of the building apparently in the first floor two white, maybe windows or whatever it shall be. And please once again - sorry for this confusion, Mr. Witness - could you please once again point to this exact point where you were working.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So when we can see at the right-hand side of this model. The witness pointed now closer to the second window we can identify to the -- from this side of the building also to the right-hand side of the building. Would this be a correct description, or would the parties have any problems with this?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, just for the record, I want to state that the witness identified it during the direct and that I think it's consistent with that aspect of it. And if counsel wants to attempt to question him on where he identified he was at, she's welcome to do so. But the description is as it was in direct and as it is now in cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, how far away from the wall of the building were you?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the wall of the building, well, I'd say -- I never measured it, so I can't tell you exactly, but it's about 4 metres, 5 metres. I mean, I didn't take a measuring tape to tell you exactly it is 4 metres or it is 5, so it's difficult for me to give you the accurate figure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. And that's an approximation of where -- how far you were away. Was there a ceremony for this delegation? Was the delegation greeted by anybody?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was working here at the time when I stopped there, so naturally people got off, went behind the building, and I went on doing my job. And I wasn't interested in that delegation. I merely heard the detainees singing Serb songs. Because I was asked to look to -- to look after the lighting. I wasn't expecting a delegation, or I didn't know when they were coming, why they would be coming, who would be coming.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that the -- can you then just use your pointer and show us again where the delegation walked, the ones you saw.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The delegation got off here, went round there, and then went westward. And I was working there. I wasn't looking after them, wasn't following them, and I couldn't know where they went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, you said that they walked down to the cafeteria restaurant building and then turned left and walked along the front of the cafeteria building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are slightly off the mark. They went here. This is the northern direction. And this is then towards west. This part over here is the restaurant, not this part, and they moved from this side and then went on. That is, down the building and then moved on. And I couldn't really keep my eye on them, and I wasn't really interested to know where they were going or why they were going.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, just leaving aside north and west and -- did you see any security persons with the delegation?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They had escorts with them. That is, there were armed guys. And they went -- they got off their cars. The cars stayed where they were. The drivers stayed in the cars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to move now to another topic. I've finished with that photograph. Sir, you testified about the water and that the drinking water came from a well and there was industrial water also that came from the River Gomjenica. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the guards have access to this industrial water supply?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean "guards"? Guards guarding the facility?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The guards at the camp who were guarding the detainees, you said that they were all around the buildings.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around buildings, yes. But they had access to that industrial water. We called it the washing point. It wasn't drinking water. It was water to wash. So yes, I suppose they did. Why not? Some washed their cars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see evidence of crimes being committed in the Omarska camp when you were working there?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I worked there, in the early days of the camp - once again, I can't say anything date-wise, because I didn't keep the record - but in the early -- in the first days, I saw several bodies. And if you could give me back the picture, then I could show you where I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, this is a copy of S15-2. And I would like to ask the witness to mark on this photograph where he saw the bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We can -- let's first hear the testimony, and then let's agree whether it's necessary to mark it or to describe it. Could you please answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you said in the first days you saw several bodies. Where were those bodies?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bodies were on the northern side of the restaurant, somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, you're pointing as we look at the photograph to the left-hand side in front of the left-hand side of the cafeteria restaurant building; is that correct? Before the -- before you see the lawned area. Are you pointing to the area to the left-hand side of the cafeteria on the cemented area before the grass? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the lawn, on the grass. If we are looking west -- if I turned westward, then it is to the right of the restaurant. I don't know from where you are looking or if you are looking from the west when you say "left." To my mind, this is to the right of the restaurant, if we're looking in the east-west direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think now it's really necessary that we mark this point because it will be extremely difficult to follow at this time the testimony without in further marks on it. And it's for the Defence to come back to this later on if they so want. Because the last time we got a clear explanation and it transpires from the transcript, but here it's no longer possible to follow. This would be then S15-2-2. If the witness would please take a marker and mark the position where he believes ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean, I cannot do it down to an inch, but it's here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark next to the circle that you've just drawn the number "1."

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many bodies did you see?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there were five, maybe six. It was a long time ago. I don't know how well my memory still serves me. But it was thereabouts. Once again, I did not write it down to tell you whether there were exactly five or exactly six.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so we're crystal clear, these were dead bodies, were they not?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other bodies while you were working in the Omarska camp, any other dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them later on. But once again, I cannot tell you how much later. Later on, however, I saw two more bodies in front of the white house. I never went near it. It was -- I was going this way. I was going down this pavement performing my jobs, and I did not -- I could not come closer because the police would not let me to do that and for my own safety's sake I had no wish to go near it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you take the marker and draw again where you saw those bodies and put next to that the number "2."

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see on any other occasion dead bodies in the camp?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, I never saw bodies again. It was only on those two occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you testified in the Omarska trial on the 6th of February, 2001, do you recall saying - and this is for Defence and Your Honours at page 7447 - do you recall stating then that you said, "On more than one occasion, I saw one or two dead bodies near the white house"?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's it. I saw two bodies. Perhaps it was interpreted, worded different. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked in the Omarska trial -- I will just put the questions and answers to you. You were asked: Did you ever have an opportunity to see bodies? And you said -- answer: At the very beginning of the functioning of the camp, I saw several dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, the page number and --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. 7446.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said: Answer: "They were located behind the kitchen building. That is, behind the restaurant of the mine near the pit. There were some containers on the northern side of the complex."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I have an objection to the attempt by counsel to use this transcript for purposes of impeachment. It's rather clear if you read it in context, starting from page 7446, when this witness previously testified consistent that he saw --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, no argument. If you want to have a broader scope that should be read out, please tell the other party.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's not a question. I'm basing my objection because she's already asked the question. If the Court reads the question that counsel omitted to on page 7446, line 25, and then reads specifically the answer of the witness, I think it will be clear for all of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm trying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I understand your objection in this way, that you want -- that both the question and the answer be read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Specifically -- -- specifically the prior questions as well. Because I believe that it's misleading and mischaracterises prior testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In order to avoid that we have to come back to this issue later on, I'll ask the Prosecution to start at that point on page 7446. The Defence believes it's necessary to start with the line of questioning. Could you indicate the line.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can, Your Honour. It commences on line 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do you have problems with starting with line 15?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. And I was taking the witness to the very question and answer that the Defence objected to in the middle of my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I will start again, and I will read in relation to what the questions and answers that were put to you in relation to seeing dead bodies in the Omarska camp when you testified two years ago. The question was: "Mr. Vuleta, throughout these 20 days that you spent in the Omarska camp, did you ever have an opportunity to see bodies?" Your answer was: "Yes." You were asked: "When?" You answered: "At the very beginning of the functioning of the camp, I saw several dead bodies." You were asked: "Where were they?" You replied: "They were located behind the kitchen building, that is, behind the restaurant of the mine near the pit. There were some containers on the northern side of the complex." You were then asked: "Later on did you ever see any bodies again?" You replied: "Yes. On more -- on one more occasion I saw one or two dead bodies near the white house." And I apologise to counsel and the Court. So it was only those two occasions --

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, isn't it the same, what you read and what I said? You were mentioning some containers at the mine, at the pit, but there are no containers here, so there is something wrong with the interpretation. But I said the same thing. Perhaps you have in mind some containers and that there were bodies in containers, but there are no containers. I said that there was a container -- a pump collecting sewage, and perhaps you confused that with the container containing bodies. So perhaps -- why, we're talk at cross-purposes. To the north, behind the restaurant, there is a pump which collects sewage waters and then pumps it out. So perhaps -- and that we also call containers, so perhaps that's why a misunderstanding arose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. You said that you worked 24 hours on and had 48 hours off and that you slept in the electrical workshop.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were approximately 1.000 to 2.000 detainees kept in the hangar building, were there not, on the first floor and the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these are some general estimates that I made. I didn't count those men, nor did I have any lists to know exactly. So these are some approximate figures. From what I could see or what I estimated, but it need not be accurate. I mean, if I see a throng of people in the street, I cannot really say whether there were 500 or 550 or 400. But generally speaking, a rough approximation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the night-time, did you ever hear cries and screams coming from within the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not hear anything, because I slept. As I've explained it, if you can give me the marker, and I will draw the area where I was. And the walls are thick there, so I simply couldn't possibly hear anything. And besides, I live in a rural area. I work a lot. I really get tired. And when I fall asleep, I simply can't hear anything. It's not as if you could hear something from behind the wall here. I just couldn't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the electrical workshop was in the corner on the ground floor of the hangar building, as you looked towards it.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other detainees detained in the rooms near the electrical workshop?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the adjacent room. Yes, there was a certain number of detainees there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
